scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The stolen dance that won the cake.
This is the cakewalk, spanning the mid-19th century to the early 20th century.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The cakewalk develops from mid-19th-century prize walks on Southern plantations in the United States, and exhibits at the 1876 Centennial Exposition in Philadelphia.
It moves into minstrel shows and eventually onto Broadway, starring performers like Dora Dean and Charles E. Johnson, before becoming an international sensation in Paris in 1903.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: People perform it during Sunday gatherings and nighttime parties as a recreational pastime and a covert satire of white aristocratic European dances, while slaveholders award cakes to the winning couples.
Today, it is a revived tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: It is a lively partnered vernacular jazz dance featuring processional walking, high-stepping kicks, struts, slides, and an erect upper body tilted backward, alternating with frantic jumps and turns.
Watch for the high-stepping strut and the chalkline walk.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is notated in a 2/4 time signature with an oompah rhythm, incorporating syncopation, polyrhythms, and habanera rhythms.
Historically played with banjos and violins, it heavily shapes the development of ragtime.
Listen for the banjo and the violin.
The pulse is 2/4.
It is a lively 2/4 march with a heavy oompah beat, enriched by syncopated ragtime rhythms, banjos, and violins.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear handed-down finery including top hats, swallow-tail coats, large bow ties, canes, and long ruffled hoop skirts.
Settings range from plantation yards to rented halls with banked spectator tiers.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Key figures include Dora Dean, Charles E. Johnson, Tom Fletcher, Eugénie Fougère, Aida Overton Walker, and Will Marion Cook.
The dance spreads from Florida across Georgia, the Carolinas, Virginia, and New York, reaching international popularity in Paris and influencing early tango styles in Buenos Aires.
It is rooted in African American plantation culture, influenced by the ring shout, and serves as a direct precursor and sibling style to ragtime music.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken
Variant names as a small list

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: The cakewalk influences ragtime, as many early ragtime tunes are actually cakewalks that share identical musical antecedents.
The cakewalk shares music with the tango, since the arrival of the cakewalk and ragtime in Buenos Aires in 1903 influences early styles of tango.
The cakewalk is a variant of the lindy hop, with early 1900s cakewalk steps preserved and performed within the modern lindy hop community.

scenes.title: Welcome
narration: Chapter 1 covers first steps. Today, you will learn the processional partner walk and erect posture.
